title: Kolkata (Batch 2)
selection: Batch 2. Kolkata had only overview, things to do and highlights. Adds how to reach, local transport, best time, food, who it's for, common mistakes and FAQs, a fuller overview (pending review) and rewrites the draft kolkata-3-days itinerary (moved here from state-gaps.json). places.name: Kolkata

places.seoTitle: Kolkata Travel Guide: Sights, Food & Durga Puja
places.seoDescription: Plan Kolkata: Victoria Memorial, Howrah Bridge, Dakshineswar and Kalighat, Belur Math, the Indian Museum, College Street and Durga Puja.

overview.text:
Kolkata, the former Calcutta, lies on the east bank of the Hooghly and calls itself the cultural capital of India. It was the capital of British India, and its centre still shows it: the white-marble Victoria Memorial at the end of the Maidan, the vast green 'lungs of Kolkata', and the steel Howrah Bridge over the river.

The city is also deeply Bengali. Tagore's family home at Jorasanko is a museum, the bookstalls and Coffee House of College Street are still busy, and in Kumartuli potters shape the clay idols for Durga Puja, the city's great festival every September–October. Kali is worshipped at Kalighat and Dakshineswar, and Belur Math across the river is the home of the Ramakrishna movement. Food is a reason to come in itself, from machher jhol and roshogolla to phuchka, kati rolls and Chinatown's Indian Chinese. Come in winter for the mildest weather.

how_to_reach.text:
By air: Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport at Dum Dum is about 16 km north-east of the centre and has domestic and international flights.

By train: long-distance trains arrive at Howrah, India's largest railway complex, or Sealdah, with Kolkata, Shalimar and Santragachi stations for some routes. Check which station your train uses: Howrah is across the river from the city centre.

local_transport.text: The Kolkata Metro, running since 1984, is the quickest way to beat traffic along the north–south spine. Yellow metered taxis, app cabs and auto rickshaws cover the rest, and ferries cross the Hooghly between Kolkata and Howrah, which is a pleasant way to reach the riverside temples and see the waterfront. Cycle and hand-pulled rickshaws still work short trips in some older neighbourhoods.

best_time.text: Winter (roughly November–February) is the most comfortable time, with lows of about 9–11 °C in December and January. Summer (March–June) is hot and humid, and the monsoon brings heavy rain from June to September. Come in September–October for Durga Puja, the city's biggest festival, but book early and expect crowds. Poila Boishak (the Bengali New Year), Kali Puja, Diwali, Christmas and Eid are also celebrated.

items.title: Culture lovers
items.body: Jorasanko Thakur Bari, the Indian Museum, the Victoria Memorial and College Street's Coffee House.

items.title: Food lovers
items.body: Bengali fish, sweets, street food and Park Street's restaurants.

items.title: Festival-goers
items.body: Durga Puja in September–October, and Kumartuli's idol-makers in the weeks before.
Assuming every train uses Howrah. Many arrive at Sealdah, on the other side of the river.
Taking a taxi everywhere at rush hour. The metro is often much faster.
Arriving for Durga Puja without a hotel booking.
Leaving without trying the sweets. Roshogolla, sandesh and mishti dohi are a big part of the city's food culture.

items.title: How far is the airport from the city centre?
items.body: About 16 km; the airport is at Dum Dum, north-east of the centre.

items.title: When is Durga Puja?
items.body: In September–October; the exact dates follow the Hindu calendar.

items.title: What is the best way to get around?
items.body: The metro for longer hops, with taxis, autos and Hooghly ferries for the rest.

items.title: When is the weather best?
items.body: Winter, when December–January lows are about 9–11 °C. Summers are hot and humid, and June–September is the monsoon.

plan.overview: A first visit that mixes the colonial centre, the riverside temples and old north Kolkata, with a Bengali meal every day. Use the metro and ferries to dodge traffic.
plan.style: City break: heritage, temples and food
plan.start: Kolkata (airport about 16 km from the centre)
plan.season: Winter is most comfortable; September–October for Durga Puja. Summer is hot and humid, and June–September is the monsoon.
plan.difficulty: Easy; lots of walking in heat and crowds
plan.transport: Metro, taxis, autos and Hooghly ferries
